source.title: Authors Guild — Model Trade Book Contract, section 5 Royalties
source.fullContextOnce: The Model Contract uses suggested retail list price for one hardcover schedule. For most small and medium-sized publishers it defines Net Receipts as amounts actually received by the publisher minus only return credits and applicable taxes, postage, and shipping. The commentary identifies list/cover price and publisher net receipts as common trade royalty bases; it says net receipts are typically amounts received after taxes and applicable bookseller or wholesaler discounts.
exactPrimaryWording: ‘all amounts actually received by Publisher, minus only return credits and applicable taxes, postage and shipping costs (hereinafter called Net Receipts)’
‘either (1) the suggested retail (otherwise known as list or cover price) of the book or (2) the publisher’s net receipts’
source.fact: Net receipts is contract-defined actual publisher receipts after specified deductions; it is not list price or net profit.

proposal.prompt: В договоре о торговой книге роялти считают с фактических поступлений издателя после предусмотренных вычетов, а не с розничной цены. Как называется эта база?
answers: Валовые поступления издателя до вычетов (gross receipts)
Чистая прибыль издателя после расходов (net profit)
Чистые поступления издателя, определённые договором (net receipts)
answerNotes: List/cover price is the suggested retail-price base.
Net profit subtracts business expenses; the Model Contract defines Net Receipts by specified credits and costs.
Net receipts is the contract term for actual amounts received less specified deductions; definitions vary by contract.
proposal.difficultyRationale: MEDIUM distinguishes four plausible contract bases—list price, gross receipts, net receipts, and net profit. It requires ordinary royalty-base understanding without math, recoupment chronology, or category elimination.

source.title: International Dunhuang Programme / British Library — Buddhist texts: The Diamond Sutra
source.locator: ‘The Diamond Sutra’ opening paragraph; ‘Colophon from the Diamond Sutra’ complete paragraph; article closing qualification. Official-site search returned text on 2026-10-16; direct open returned 403.
source.fullContextOnce: IDP identifies the Chinese Diamond Sutra copy as the world’s earliest dated printed book, made in 868 CE. Its colophon records sponsor Wang Jie and completion on 11 May 868; the text was woodblock-printed on seven yellow-dyed sheets joined into a five-metre scroll. The article qualifies the milestone: earlier printing examples exist, but 868 is the earliest date found in a complete printed text, making this copy the first example of that bounded category.
source.scopeLimit: Use earliest dated printed book / earliest date in a complete printed text. Do not claim the first printing event or first printed object of any kind.

proposal.prompt: Какой из этих буддийских текстов IDP называет самым ранним датированным печатным книжным изданием, уточняя, что 868 год — самая ранняя дата в сохранившемся полном печатном тексте?
answerNotes: IDP catalogs a Chinese Heart Sutra manuscript, not this dated-print milestone.
IDP catalogs a Lotus Sutra scroll dated 672, not the cited 868 milestone.
IDP catalogs Sukhavativyuha as a separate Buddhist sutra; the milestone is about the Diamond Sutra copy.
IDP identifies the Diamond Sutra copy with the milestone and limits it to the earliest date in a complete printed text.
proposal.difficultyRationale: MEDIUM rests on a standard book-history milestone and four real, parallel Buddhist sutra titles, not incidental artifact fittings. The wording does not claim printing began with this copy.
